statement: On a test, a wrong answer costs nothing. Kai has 4 unanswered 5-point questions, each with 5 choices. On every one he can rule out one choice he knows is wrong, and he guesses among the rest. On average, how many points will his guesses earn him?

choices.misconception: I thought a guess is worth the same as a blank, because a guess might be wrong.
I worked out that he expects 1 correct answer, 4 times 1 in 4, and forgot each one is worth 5 points.
I worked out the average for one question, 5 points times 1 in 4, and forgot there are four questions.
I used a 1 in 5 chance on each question, forgetting that he has ruled one choice out.

hints: After ruling one out, how many choices are left on each question?
With no penalty, a guess on average earns its chance of being right times the points it is worth. Add that up over all the questions.
Each guess has a 1 in 4 chance, and each question is worth 5 points, so each guess is worth 5/4 points on average.

solutions.reliable: Each question has 4 choices left, so a guess is right 1 time in 4. On average each guess earns 5 x 1/4 = 1.25 points, and four questions give 4 x 1.25 = 5 points. A blank earns 0. The transferable idea: with no penalty for a wrong answer, every guess is worth more than a blank, and ruling out a choice makes it worth even more.
solutions.elegant: Four guesses, each with a 1 in 4 chance, give one correct answer on average, and one correct answer is worth 5 points.

whyOnTest: Math Kangaroo takes nothing off for a wrong answer, so knowing what a guess is worth turns blanks into real points.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
